extraction_text: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya about the events during the night battle, specifically focusing on Drona's actions and the responses of the Pandavas and others.
Drona, enraged, enters the Srinjaya army and later charges at the Panchalas after the deaths of Sindhu's king and Bhurishravas.
The five Pandavas, along with their armies, charge at Drona during the night battle.
Drona kills the Kekayas and the sons of Shikhandi with showers of arrows.
King Shibi, enraged, charges at Drona but is killed by Drona who first kills his horses and charioteer, then beheads him.
The prince of Kalinga, angry over his father's death by Bhima, attacks Bhima in battle with arrows.
Bhima jumps from his chariot, rushes to the Kalinga prince's chariot, and kills him with his fists, scattering his bones.
Karna and the brave brothers of the Kalinga prince, enraged, shoot snake-like iron arrows at Bhima.
Bhima left his opponent's chariot and approached Dravara's chariot, punching him repeatedly while Dravara shot arrows.

attributes.outcome: Dravara was killed by Bhima and fell to the ground.

extraction_text: Bhima rushed to Jayatsena's chariot and roared like a lion in front of Karna.
Bhima grabbed Jayatsena's left arm and killed him with a slap.
Karna threw a gold-decorated spear at Bhima, who caught it smiling.
Bhima threw the spear back at Karna, but Shakuni broke it mid-air with an oil-soaked arrow.
Duryodhana's sons attacked Bhima's chariot with a dense arrow shower.
Bhima killed the charioteer and horses of Durmukha with sharp arrows, causing Durmukha to jump onto Durjaya's chariot.
Durmukha and Durjaya rode together in one chariot and shot multiple arrows at Bhima.
Bhima kicked the chariot of Durmukha and Durjaya into the ground in front of Karna, Ashwatthama, Duryodhana, Kripa, Shalya, and Vrika.
Bhima killed Durmukha and Durjaya with his fists and crushed them underfoot.
The army lamented, and kings speculated that Bhima was Rudra (Shiva) disguised, fighting the sons of Dhritarashtra.

attributes.supernatural_element: Perception of Bhima as a god

extraction_text: Kings fled in disarray, alone, without companions.

At night, after the army was devastated, Bhima was highly praised by the kings and honored by Yudhishthira, Nakula, Sahadeva, Drupada, Virata, Kekayas, and others, likened to Shiva honored by gods after Andhaka's death.
Duryodhana's sons, angry and eager for battle, along with Drona, surrounded Bhima with chariots, infantry, and elephants.
A fierce battle erupted in the dark, terrifying night among the great Kshatriya warriors, delighting jackals, crows, and vultures.
Sanjaya reported that Shalya (referred to as 'son' in context) was killed by Satyaki while sitting in fasting meditation.
Shalya became furious and accused Satyaki of abandoning Kshatriya dharma by attacking a helpless, unarmed person who had stopped fighting.

attributes.context: Shalya's son (Madrasena) had been killed by Arjuna and was sitting helpless when attacked by Satyaki

extraction_text: Shalya swore an oath that he would kill Satyaki, his sons, and his brothers before nightfall unless protected by Arjuna, or else he would go to hell.
Shalya blew his conch shell with great force, roaring like a lion.
Satyaki became enraged and reminded Shalya that his heroic son Madrasena and brother Shala had been killed.
Satyaki vowed to kill Shalya, his sons, cattle, and relatives in battle, swearing by Krishna's feet and his own good deeds.
The two heroes, eyes red with anger, began shooting arrows at each other.
Duryodhana arrived with thousands of elephants and chariots, surrounding Shalya for protection.
Shakuni, surrounded by heroic warriors, arrived with one hundred thousand cavalry to protect Shalya.
Shalya covered Satyaki with a shower of arrows while protected by powerful warriors.
Dhrishtadyumna became enraged and advanced with his army upon seeing Satyaki covered by arrows.
A massive battle erupted between the two armies with tremendous noise.
Shalya shot nine arrows at Satyaki, who responded by wounding Shalya with ten arrows.
Shalya was deeply wounded by Satyaki's arrows and fell unconscious on his chariot seat.
Seeing Shalya unconscious, his charioteer quickly carried him away from the battle.
Ashwatthama witnessed Satyaki (Satyaki) being struck by an arrow and falling unconscious.
Ashwatthama became enraged and charged toward the Satvatas (Satyaki's forces).
Ghatotkacha saw Ashwatthama charging toward Satyaki's chariot and became furious, moving to intercept him.
Ghatotkacha arrived in a terrifying eight-wheeled iron chariot covered in bear skin, drawn by non-horse, non-elephant creatures, with vulture banners and bloody decorations.
Ghatotkacha was accompanied by a fierce army of Rakshasas (demons) armed with iron weapons, stones, and trees.
Ghatotkacha appeared like Death at doomsday, terrifying the kings and Duryodhana's army.
Ghatotkacha roared like a lion, causing elephants to defecate and people to tremble.
At night, the Rakshasas grew stronger and unleashed a rain of stones, iron wheels, rockets, darts, spears, and other weapons.
The kings, Duryodhana's sons, and Karna fled in terror from the fierce battle.
Only Ashwatthama remained fearless, shooting arrows to dispel Ghatotkacha's illusions.
Ghatotkacha became enraged when his illusions were dispelled and shot terrible arrows that struck Ashwatthama.
Ashwatthama, furious, quickly shot ten arrows that struck the furious Ghatotkacha.
Ghatotkacha, deeply wounded, grabbed a flying disc with a hundred thousand spokes, sharp-edged and jeweled, and threw it at Ashwatthama to kill him.
Ashwatthama knocked the flying disc to the ground with his arrows.
Ghatotkacha covered Ashwatthama with arrows like Rahu covering the sun.
Anjanaparva (Ghatotkacha's son) intercepted the advancing Ashwatthama like a mountain blocking wind.
Ashwatthama suffered under Anjanaparva's arrows like Mount Meru suffering from cloudbursts.
Ashwatthama, brave like Rudra, Upendra (Vishnu), and Indra, calmly shot an arrow that cut Anjanaparva's banner.
Ashwatthama killed Anjanaparva's charioteer with two arrows, broke three flagpoles with three arrows, cut the bow with one arrow, and killed four horses with four arrows.
Ashwatthama destroyed Ghatotkacha's golden-studded sword with a sharp arrow.
Ashwatthama destroyed Ghatotkacha's gold-encrusted iron mace with arrows.
Ghatotkacha leaped into the air and rained down a shower of trees.
Ashwatthama shot Ghatotkacha with arrows, piercing him like sunlight through clouds.
Ghatotkacha returned to his golden chariot.
Ashwatthama killed Ghatotkacha, who wore iron armor.
Hidimba (Ghatotkacha's father) witnessed his son's death and confronted Ashwatthama.
Ashwatthama advised Hidimba to fight others instead, saying father-son combat was inappropriate.
Hidimba, enraged by his son's death, challenged Ashwatthama to fight.
Hidimba attacked Ashwatthama with axle-sized arrows.
Ashwatthama blocked Hidimba's arrow shower with his own arrows.
Hidimba created an illusion of a mountain with waterfalls of weapons.
Ashwatthama destroyed the mountain illusion with the Vajra weapon.
瓶首 (Bhima's son Ghatotkacha) transformed into a dark cloud carrying rainbows and unleashed a rain of stones upon 德罗纳之子 (Drona's son Ashwatthama).
Ashwatthama used the wind-god weapon to disperse the dark cloud.
Ashwatthama covered all directions with countless arrows, annihilating 100,000 chariot warriors.
Ashwatthama saw Ghatotkacha advancing calmly in his chariot, surrounded by numerous Rakshasas.
Duryodhana became anxious seeing Ghatotkacha and the fierce Rakshasas advancing.
Ashwatthama reassured Duryodhana, promising to eliminate his enemies and prevent defeat.
Duryodhana praised Ashwatthama's loyalty and magnanimity.
Duryodhana ordered Shakuni to lead 60,000 elephants against Arjuna, with support from multiple warriors including Karna, Drona, and others.
Duryodhana instructed Shakuni to kill Bhima, Nakula, Sahadeva, and Yudhishthira.
Shakuni advanced toward the enemy army, eager to please Duryodhana's sons by destroying the Pandavas.
Ashwatthama engaged in a fierce night battle with Ghatotkacha, compared to Indra fighting Prahlada.
Ghatotkacha angrily shot ten powerful arrows that struck Ashwatthama's chest.
Ashwatthama trembled in his chariot after being hit by Ghatotkacha's arrows.
Ghatotkacha broke Ashwatthama's radiant bow with a single arrow.
Drona's son (Ashwatthama) took up another powerful bow and showered arrows like rain.
Kripi's son (Ashwatthama) shot golden-feathered arrows at the flying Rakshasas.
The Rakshasa army became chaotic under the arrow strikes.
Ashwatthama destroyed the Rakshasa army with arrows, including horses, charioteers, and chariots.
Among thousands of Pandava kings, only the Rakshasa king Ghatotkacha dared to look at Ashwatthama.
Ghatotkacha, angry with red eyes, ordered his charioteer to take him to Ashwatthama.
Ghatotkacha charged at Ashwatthama for a one-on-one duel.
The angry Rakshasa threw an eight-wheeled discus at Ashwatthama.
Ashwatthama jumped from his chariot, caught the discus, and threw it back at Ghatotkacha.
The discus destroyed Ghatotkacha's chariot with horses, charioteer, and banner, then split the earth.
All beings praised Ashwatthama's feat of catching the weapon.
Bhima's son (Ghatotkacha) boarded Shikhandi's chariot and shot sharp arrows at Ashwatthama's chest.
Shikhandi also shot golden-feathered arrows at Ashwatthama's chest.
Ashwatthama shot thousands of iron arrows at them, but they were all cut down.
An intense battle erupted between the two lion-like men (Ghatotkacha and Shikhandi) and Ashwatthama.
Bhima arrived with an army of chariots, elephants, and cavalry.
Ashwatthama continued fighting calmly against Bhima's Rakshasa son (Ghatotkacha), Shikhandi, and their followers.
Ashwatthama displayed astonishing prowess that was difficult for all beings to achieve.
In the blink of an eye, Ashwatthama destroyed the Rakshasa army with arrows.
Ashwatthama created a river of blood with his arrows during battle.

attributes.supernatural_elements: The battlefield is described metaphorically as a terrifying river with various gruesome features.
